processing: Made as a Wuyi rock tea with shaking, partial oxidation and roasting. One seller describes a lot roasted four times.
harvest_season: Spring; little more is recorded for this bush.
appearance_dry: Twisted strips in green and brown, as one seller describes them.
appearance_liquor: Typical of roasted Wuyi oolongs: clear orange to amber.
appearance_wet: Typical of the class: green-brown leaves with darker edges.
taste_profile: One seller's notes give toasted biscuit, golden syrup and red fruit, with milky-floral aroma and a cool sweetness in the middle steeps. It is a single lot's description, not a settled profile.

brewing.notes: The usual approach for Wuyi rock teas. The middle steeps are said to be the richest, so do not stop early.

vintage_note: Sold in small lots by spring harvest year and roast, as other Wuyi famous bushes are. One seller advises resting it a year after roasting before drinking, a common view for well-fired rock teas.
description:
Yu Qi Lin, Jade Qilin, is a Wuyi famous bush named for the shape of the tree, which is said to resemble the auspicious beast of Chinese myth. It is the shape, and not the flavour, that gave it the name.

The making follows the class: shaking, partial oxidation and roasting. One seller describes four rounds of roasting for its lot, which gives some idea of the care possible, though not a rule.

That same seller reports toasted biscuit, syrup and red fruit, with roses and bamboo leaf in the early steeps, then cooler sweetness and a long finish. Brew it hot and short, and give it many steeps.

Some accounts place it among the ten famous Wuyi bushes, though such lists vary. Ask the seller for the year and the growing area. Jiu Long Ke is one named source.
history:
Chinese accounts of Wuyi tea list Yu Qi Lin among bushes named for tree form. Modern listings also include it among Wuyi's lesser-known named bushes.

A modern account of Wuyi bushes mentions it among those being expanded in demonstration plots. When it was first recorded and who first selected it is not well documented.
